readme:
# PLACEHOLDER

**This machine is a placeholder.** It is here so the community collection is not empty, and it will be removed with the first community contribution.

Have you built a machine of your own? Share it: press **Export**, and open a pull request on [exuarch-machines](https://github.com/olebru/exuarch-machines) with the file and an entry in `index.json`. The repository's README says how. Your machine takes this one's place.

## What it is

The minimal CPU you get from **New…**: a [program counter](exuarch:device/pc), [memory](exuarch:device/mem), the [instruction register](exuarch:device/ir), a [status register](exuarch:device/status) and a [clock](exuarch:device/clk) on one bus. It has a fetch routine and NOP, JMP and HLT. It also has an [LCD](exuarch:device/lcd) and one instruction more: [CHR](exuarch:instruction/CHR) prints the character written after it.

## Things to try

1. Run [Hello from the placeholder](<exuarch:program/Hello from the placeholder>) in [Run](exuarch:tab/Run).
2. Change the text, and run it again.
3. Build something better, and share it.

fetch.description: Load the opcode at the program counter into the instruction register and step past it

instructions.description: Print the character written after CHR on the LCD
